result.title: GoldiBench: Right Tools, Wrong Amount -- Benchmarking Agents on Effect Judgement in Professional Editing
result.summary: Real editing requests describe a look, not the steps to reach it, so an agent that serves them must judge how much of each tool the look takes. Existing benchmarks do not measure this: their tasks either state the tools and values, or leave the amount open and are scored by VLM judges that pass more than half of half- and triple-strength results. We introduce GoldiBench, a benchmark of 500 editing tasks in five professional applications (darktable, RawTherapee, GIMP, Inkscape, Blender), solvable by writing a program or by operating the GUI. Each task pairs a START image with a TARGET rendered from a hidden program, so the amount is fixed by a known target; the agent's edit is re-rendered and compared with TARGET, and the same task is posed with the tools and values, the tools only, or the goal only, separating operation from effect judgement. Across 25 open, GUI and closed models, agents operate well (99-100% with programs from 4B up when told the values) but fall off a cliff when they must judge the amount: given only the tools, the best model passes 19% of the tasks with programs and 33% through the GUI, and scale does not close the gap. Manuals barely help; the measured TARGET-START difference more than doubles the pass rate, but the same difference shown as an image does not for open models. Allowed four renders, agents almost always stop after the first; forced to compare, the strong models double their pass rate. Agents know the tools, but neither read nor check the amount.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 GoldiBench，用 500 个专业编辑任务（给出 START 图与隐藏程序渲染的 TARGET），并将同一任务分别以「工具+数值」「仅工具」「仅目标描述」三种形式给出，以分离「会操作」与「能判断效果强度」，评测 25 个模型后发现它们在工具操作上近乎满分，但需自行判断改动量时通过率骤降，且几乎不做多次渲染比较。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接诊断 agent 能否读取视觉差异证据来校准改动量并据此迭代、停止，与 LOOK/STOP 的收益成本和多轮验证机制高度相关；其中「被强制比较后通过率翻倍」「只渲一次就停」可为迭代式视觉反馈与验证策略提供可核查线索。
